The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Sambasiva Rao Naidu

Judgment:

The petitioners/claimants in MVOP.No.525 of 2016 on the file of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (for short 'MACT') Cum V Addl. District Judge, Ranga Reddy, being aggrieved by the order of the Tribunal dated 30-01-2018, where under, their petition for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- on account of the death of Nagulapalli Srinivas in a road traffic accident was partly allowed awarding a sum of Rs.10,28,125/-, preferred this Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'M.V. Act') and sought for enhancement of the compensation on the following grounds.

entities.text: Cum V Addl. District Judge, Ranga Reddy
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The Court below failed to appreciate the oral and documentary evidence produced by them.
The Tribunal was not justified in considering their claim that the deceased was earning sufficient amount and not justified in granting only an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards transport charges.
They have also claimed that the tribunal was not justified in not granting any amount towards damages to the clothing and articles and ought to have awarded at least a sum of Rs.5,000/-.
The 2 SSRN, J tribunal was not justified in granting Rs.15,000/- for funeral expenses instead of Rs.30,000/-.
They have also claimed that the tribunal ought to have allowed their claim and ought to have awarded Rs.1,00,000/- towards compensation for loss of estate.
While questioning the other amounts awarded by the tribunal, the appellants have sought for enhancement of the compensation from Rs.10,28,125/- to Rs.15,00,000/-.

3. According to their petition before the tribunal, it seems MVOP.No.525 of 2016 has been filed by the appellants, who are wife, daughter and parents of the deceased and they have claimed that on 21-05-2016, the said Srinivas (herein after will be referred as 'deceased') went to Kirana shop, Pargi for unloading material in a DCM Van bearing No.AP 23 W 9844.
The appellants have claimed that when the deceased stood by the side of the Van, the driver drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed him due to which he received grievous injuries.
He was immediately shifted to Government Hospital, Pargi from which he was taken to Osmania General Hospital, Hyderabad, but he succumbed to the injuries.
The appellants have filed the said OP against the owner, driver and insurer of the said vehicle.

The 3rd 3 SSRN, J respondent/driver of the vehicle remained ex parte,
whereas, owner and the insurer of the vehicle opposed the claim, they filed their separate counters disputing the material averments made by the appellants herein.

The tribunal has framed the following four issues:
1. Whether the accident occurred on 21-05-2016 at about 1430 hours at Gunj Road,
Pargi, Ranga Reddy District due to rash and negligent driving of DCM Van bearing No.AP 23 W 9844 by its driver?

3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from which respondents?
4.

4. , During enquiry, on behalf of appellants, two witnesses were examined and Exs.
A1 to A6 were marked.
The respondents did not examine any witness but marked the copy of policy as Ex.B1.
The tribunal having appreciated the oral and documentary evidence and on appreciation of the respective arguments, allowed the petition in part and awarded Rs.10,28,125/-.
5. Heard both parties.
4 SSRN, J 6.

Now the points for consideration are :
1. Whether the contentions of the appellants that the appropriate amounts were awarded under different heads can be considered, if so, whether the same can be enhanced?

2. Whether the Court below was wrong in assessing the loss of dependency and whether it came to an incorrect conclusion resulting the award of meagre amount to the appellants?
7.
As could be seen from the impugned order, it is quite clear that the appellants have claimed before the Court below that that deceased was working in a Kirana shop.
They have also claimed that the deceased was a contract labour as sweeper in Gram Panchayat, Pargi.

Even though, no acceptable evidence is placed before the Court, the tribunal considering the evidence, age of the deceased and the fact that by the time of accident, he went to a Kirana shop for unloading the stock concluded that he was working in shop as a daily wage labour or coolie and assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.5,500/- (Rs.4,000/- + Rs.1500/-).

8. The tribunal having considered the settled proposition of law in various judgments including the judgment in 'National Insurance company Vs. Pranay 5 SSRN, J Sethi and others 1' added 25% of the above income towards future prospects and considered the average income of the deceased as Rs.6,875/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellants could not place any material to show that the deceased was earning more than the above referred income.

It is not their case that the deceased was a permanent Government employee nor they have filed any documentary proof to show that the deceased was earning more than the amount that was considered by the tribunal.

sentences.text:
The award further shows that the learned Chairman keeping in view of the judgment in 'Pranay Sethi' case supra, in view has awarded Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium and in addition to the same, awarded sum of Rs.30,000/- towards love and affection.
10.
Therefore, absolutely there are no grounds to enhance the compensation amount.

As per the observations made by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'Pranay Sethi' case supra, maximum amount that can be awarded under loss of consortium, loss of estate, funeral expenses was aptly 2017 16 SCC 680 6 SSRN, J followed and was awarded by the tribunal, as such, there are no merits and appeal is liable to be dismissed.
11.
In the result, the appeal is dismissed.
Consequently, Miscellaneous applications if any, are closed.
No costs.
SAMBASIVA RAO NAIDU, J 15th February 2024.
